title: Mid-Level Propulsion Safety Risk Analysis Engineer

cond_0001.intro:
[Company name masked] is looking to bring on a Mid-Level Propulsion Safety Risk Analysis Engineer to join the team.
The successful candidate should be able to work collaboratively as part of a team and be detailed oriented, enthusiastic, self-directed, capable of managing multiple projects/competing priorities, able to communicate complex topics effectively, and have an ability/desire to learn and grow technically.
cond_0001.responsibilities: Perform risk analyses and other statistical analyses to support all [Company name masked] Programs with respect to propulsion in-service safety and reliability. Evaluate and support supplier (mainly engine companies) risk and statistical assessments with a focus on assessing the validity of their technical and statistical assumptions. Provide statistical analysis support and collaborate with Industry committees. Collaborate with Propulsion Safety and Risk Analysis Experts to develop new tools and approaches for analyzing safety and reliability risks.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited course of study in engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics or chemistry
3+ Years of experience performing quantitative or statistical analysis, data collection, preparation and interpretation
3+ Years of experience with scripting programming languages such as Python, MATLAB, or similar
1+ Years of experience in performing risk assessments and risk management
Solid understanding of statistical distributions and model exploration
The position must meet Export Control compliance requirements, therefore a ""US Person"" as defined by 22 C.F.R. 120.15 Is required. ""US Person"" includes US Citizen, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee.
Preferred Requirements
Life Data Analysis, Reliability Growth, Monte Carlo and Fault Tree Analysis experience
Design of Experiments and Probability of Detection experience
Technical/engineering understanding of jet engine and fuel systems fundamentals (mechanically and operationally)
Experience working in query languages such as SQL
Experience with JMP, Minitab, C, Java
Data visualization tools such as Tableau
Experience in engineering modeling and/or analysis with computer programming of analytical models, simulations, and/or data processing
Education/experience typically acquired through advanced technical education from an accredited course of study in engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics or chemistry (e.g. Bachelor) and typically 5 or more years' related work experience or an equivalent combination of technical education and experience (e.g. PhD+1 years' related work experience, Master+3 years' related work experience). In [Location masked], ABET accreditation is the preferred, although not required, accreditation standard.
